whatItIs.text: The standard mushroom of the grocery aisle is the cultivated white button, Agaricus bisporus — a fungus, not a plant, grown in the dark on compost.

historyNote.text: The word mushroom may descend from the French mousseron, in reference to moss; its old rival toadstool first appeared in 14th-century England, literally a stool for toads and a warning that a fungus was not for eating.

howToChoose.text: Choose firm, dry, unblemished caps without sliminess; open veils under the cap mean more mature flavour, which some like and some avoid.

storage.text: Keep in the original packaging or a paper bag in the fridge — plastic traps moisture and they go slimy.

useItUp.text: Older mushrooms sink happily into stock, duxelles, or risotto.

substitutions.ratio: a few per handful of buttons
substitutions.note: intense savoury depth; soak, then use both
